record.file_problem: The supplied text is cut off at 400,000 characters from a 1,944,000-character document; the excerpt ends mid-section.
record.tranche_reason: The text makes a specific scope argument: fitted laws and effective exponents from repeated-corpus studies do not automatically transfer to single-pass training without matched evidence. It does not report a direct test of the claimed held-out-loss scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The study reports row-map, optimizer, PLGA, and predictive-reduction results, not measurements of held-out pretraining loss across parameter, token, or compute scales. It also does not test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation or architectural-shape effects. The only claim-relevant argument in the supplied excerpt concerns transfer across data regimes.
record.test_reason: This monograph studies PLDR-LLM row-map collapse, AdamW state dynamics, PLGA defects, predictive closure and cache reduction. In the supplied excerpt it reports no held-out pretraining loss measured across parameters, tokens or compute. It reports no compute-optimal split, no shape ablation at fixed parameter count, and no downstream-versus-scale curve. The only nearby statement is a generic caution (Section 1.5, repeated in 12.1.1): repeated-corpus fitted laws and effective exponents should not transfer to single-pass training without matched evidence. That caution concerns the author's own fluctuation and finite-size laws, not language-model loss scaling laws. It is stated as a methodological principle and is not backed by a reported comparison of loss-scaling fits, so it is neither a result nor a specific argument against any version. The study does not test the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is partly right but misdirected. The authors conclude that exact path identities, conditional dynamical statements and finite empirical findings must be kept separate. On the empirical side, the tested reduced row and optimizer states fail to close, and trained PLGA does not inherit the upstream row-constant face. Finite state-specific predictive and cache reduction succeeds. No thermodynamic critical class or PLDR universality class is identified. The data-regime caution refers to the author's own fluctuation laws; the work says nothing about language-model loss scaling laws or compute-optimal allocation.
record.recipe_differences: The study concerns PLDR row-map dynamics, optimizer state, and predictive reduction rather than measuring held-out cross-entropy scaling against model size, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The text states that data law, training schedule, resource consumption, and fitting choices matter to transfer and interpretation; it does not report claim-specific loss-scaling sensitivity tests in the supplied excerpt.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 13.1.4 (Corollary 13.7, Eq. 13.16) shows analytically that the consumed corpus fraction rescales variance-based training fluctuation powers (N^γ becomes γ−ω). The argument is that fitted exponents under a repeated corpus should not be transferred to a single pass by relabelling the update axis. This concerns fluctuation and susceptibility exponents of internal observables, not held-out loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fitted scaling exponents of training-fluctuation observables depend on the data-presentation law (repeated versus single-pass, consumed fraction).

rows.subject: Repeated-corpus and single-pass training laws

rows.measure: Transferability of fitted scaling laws across training data regimes
rows.value: Not automatically transferable without matched evidence.
rows.note: This is a scope argument, not a reported comparison of held-out-loss scaling fits.
rows.check: This row is not a result: it is a general methodological caution (Sections 1.5 and 12.1.1) with no measurement, baseline or value. The 'laws' it refers to are the author's own fitted fluctuation and susceptibility laws for PLDR training, not held-out loss power laws in other modalities or regimes. It therefore does not bear on V5, and a 'partial' state is unsupported. Drop the row or relink it to none.
